name: Guiamala
body:
GUIAMALA
CR 5

This towering quadruped stands over 20 feet tall, resembling a cross between a giraffe and a dromedary camel, spotted brown, tawny, and white, with a long brush-like tail, with a head crowned with horns.

XP 1,600
NG Huge magical beast
Init +5; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 10, flat-footed 16 (+1 Dex, +1 dodge, +8 natural, –2 size)
hp 59 (7d10+21)
Fort +8, Ref +6, Will +5 Resist negative energy 10

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee 2 hooves +9 (1d6+4), gore +4 (2d6+2)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 5 ft. (10 ft. with gore)
Special Attacks haboob

STATISTICS

Str 19, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 5, Wis 12, Cha 15
Base Atk +7; CMB +13; CMD 25
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Mobility
Skills Perception +10, Survival +2
SQ refreshing lick, walkover, water finder

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Haboob (Su)

Once per hour, the guiamala can call upon the spirits of the dust to protect it, calling up roiling, stationary cloud of swirling dust and sand in a 40-foot radius centered on itself. This haboob provides concealment within 5 feet and total concealment beyond 5 feet except to the guiamala. In addition, other creatures entering or beginning their turn within it are lashed by driven grit, taking 2d6 points of slashing damage (DC 15 Reflex half). Creatures failing their save are also blinded for 1 round.

The save DC is Charisma-based.

Refreshing Lick (Su)

A guiamala made friendly can lick a living creature as a full-round action, affecting them as lesser restoration and cure light wounds (CL 7). A creature can’t benefit from any guiamala’s refreshing lick again for 24 hours.

Walkover (Ex)

A guiamala can move through the space of Medium or smaller creatures (or similar-sized obstacles) without provoking attacks of opportunity, except from creatures wielding reach weapons.

Water Finder (Su)

A guiamala can sense the presence of water at will, as if it had cast locate object (CL 7).

ECOLOGY

Environment warm desert and plains
Organization solitary, pair, or herd (1–4 guiamalas and 3–18 camels or giraffes)
Treasure none

The guiamala is believed by some to be a simple herbivore of the dry plains, but tales tell of its ability to sense water in a parched land. The sight of the creature is believed to be a good omen, and only the wicked would harm these gentle creatures. Those that befriend and travel with the guiamala do not suffer thirst and their vitality is ever renewed by the creature’s presence. Those who anger them can be swept up in a dust storm and left for dead.

Its legs stretch 10 feet high, allowing it to step over obstacles with ease. Its neck is long but flexible and is crowned with a nest of short brown or black horns. While not aggressive, it can use these to defend itself. It prefers to let its swift cloven hooves carry it away from danger.

Guiamalas are solitary by nature but sometimes travel in company with giraffes other herbivores of the savannah.
